The issue was that `rich.console.Console().print(end="...")` incorrectly printed a newline instead of the specified `end` string when no positional arguments were provided. This happened because `Console.print` defaulted to `objects = (NewLine(),)` when `objects` was empty. The fix changes `objects = (NewLine(),)` to `objects = ("",)` in both `Console.print` and `Console.log`. This forces the execution path through the `Text` processing logic, ensuring that the `end` parameter is correctly applied and rendered, matching the behavior of Python's built-in `print()` function.
